How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (8)

  1. How many people work on the Apono product within 1Password, and how has that changed since the acquisition?
    Headcount indicates whether the team behind the product has been kept together after the acquisition.
  2. Have there been any workforce reductions at Apono before or since its acquisition by 1Password?
    Workforce reductions after an acquisition bear on support quality.
  3. Has Apono or 1Password been subject to any regulatory investigation, order or penalty in the last five years?
    Regulatory action against an access-control vendor bears on a bank's own supervisory standing.
  4. Is Apono or 1Password party to any pending or recently resolved material litigation?
    Material litigation can affect the vendor.
  5. Has Apono had any security incident or published vulnerability affecting its service, connector or customer environments?
    A service that grants privileged access is a high-value target.
  6. Has Apono lost any notable customer since the acquisition was announced?
    Customer departures can signal product or service problems.
  7. Are Apono's two co-founders still leading the product within 1Password, and on what terms?
    Founder retention after an acquisition affects the product's direction.
  8. What are Apono's plans, licensing units and list prices, and will they change under 1Password?
    Price and licensing units are needed to compare the product with alternatives.

Timeline

  1. 2026-06-15 · acquisition Apono
    1Password acquires Apono

    1Password announced on 2026-06-15 that it had acquired Apono and would combine its just-in-time access capabilities with 1Password Unified Access and a new credential broker. Terms were not disclosed; SecurityWeek reported on 2026-06-17 that Calcalist put the price at $250 million to $300 million. The announcement does not say whether Apono continues as a standalone product; Apono's site describes it as now part of 1Password. 1Password (other, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)SecurityWeek (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)Apono (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)

  2. 2025-11-18 · funding Apono
    Apono raises $34 million Series B

    SecurityWeek reported on 2025-11-18 that Apono had raised a $34 million Series B led by USVP with 33N, Swisscom Ventures, Vertex Ventures and earlier investors, taking total funding to more than $54 million, and named Intel, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Workday as customers.
